pi.summary: Control — Core of the control loop
pi.text:
Controls the output power so that the grid connection sits at the offset (grid power: positive = import, negative = export). In zones 1 and 2 either the PI controller computes it, where P reacts to the current deviation and I compensates a persistent one, or the setpoint calculation, which forms the new setpoint in one step from the actual power. Deviations within the dead band trigger no action. After each action the regulation waits for the wait time, with adaptive wait time only until the actual power reaches the setpoint.

The integral is limited against windup, mostly reset on zone changes and slowly reduced within the dead band. Several instances share the deviation according to the distribution mode ("Distribution" tab).

If the inverter does not follow the setpoint at the limit, the regulation rewrites it and, if necessary, brings the device back via rest mode (stall detection). It keeps the device's remote control active by renewing the remote control timeout regularly. The periodic trigger additionally starts the regulation at a fixed interval.

Starting point: the defaults P = 1.3, I = 0.05. If the output power oscillates, lower P; if it follows too slowly, raise P; if a deviation persists, raise I.

zones.summary: SOC Zone Logic — behaviour based on battery state of charge
zones.text:
Zone 0 (surplus, optional): SOC ≥ export threshold AND PV surplus → output at Hard Limit Z0. Discharge current 2 A. PI integral frozen. Always sits on top of an active Zone-1 cycle; on exit the zone is re-derived from the SOC, during Tariff Lock or battery priority control rests.

Zone 1 (aggressive): SOC > zone-1 threshold → high discharge current, offset 1 (Night Offset while dark, optional). Runs through until SOC ≤ zone-3 threshold — no yo-yo effect.

Zone 1 night forcing (optional): starts Zone 1 while dark already below the zone-1 threshold if the PV forecast refills the battery the next day.

Zone 2 (conservative): zone-3 < SOC ≤ zone-1 → 0 A discharge current, dynamic output limit (min(Hard Limit Z1, max(0, PV − reserve))), offset 2.

Zone 3 (safety stop): SOC ≤ zone-3 threshold → output 0 W, rest mode (default mode '0'). AC charging remains possible.

Multi-instance: while another instance of the same grid group charges (AC, tariff or grid charging), Zone 1 uses the Zone 2 output limit — the battery does not discharge, PV is still fed in. A grid group charges or discharges, never both.

Target charging: while charging with house priority, the output limit PV − PV reserve also applies in Zone 1; with battery priority Zone 1 and Zone 2 do not start (case ZB).

surplus.text:
Zone 0 feeds in the PV surplus at Hard Limit Z0 with a full battery instead of curtailing it. After charging to the target it has the highest priority and blocks tariff charging, Tariff Lock and AC charging meanwhile.

Zone 0 starts from the SOC threshold as soon as PV exceeds consumption plus hysteresis. If the inverter throttles PV to 0 W at a full battery, the PV=0 entry starts Zone 0 even at PV = 0; it is protected against toggling. Zone 0 ends when PV drops below consumption or the SOC drops below the threshold minus SOC hysteresis. Afterwards Zone 1 or 2 continues, depending on the SOC.

Optionally, with the PV forecast Zone 0 starts on high-yield days before the battery is full, as soon as PV exceeds Hard Limit Z0. The exit lock keeps Zone 0 through short clouds while the power forecast is high enough.

The SOC threshold must be above the zone-1 threshold and should be about 5 % below the app charge limit. Zone 3 ends Zone 0 at any time; while charging to the target it is blocked.

ac.summary: AC charge — grid charges the battery
ac.text:
AC charging charges the battery when power would be exported at the grid connection even without own discharging, e.g. from a second PV system (case G). The charge power follows the surplus without PI in one step, between minimum charge power and max. charge power. Charging ends at the charge target, when the surplus disappears or when the option is switched off (case H). Afterwards Zone 1 or 2 continues, depending on the SOC. Case I clears any contradiction between mode and charging session.

AC charging does not start during Zone 0 or tariff charging; Zone 3 keeps protecting. If several instances charge at the same time, they form their own AC pool, weighted by the room left to the charge target. The other instances of the grid group meanwhile only discharge PV. During target charging, AC charging only starts if it is enabled there as a charging source.

tariff.summary: Tariff Arbitrage (Tibber, aWATTar …) — three price tiers
tariff.text:
Tariff control aligns charging and discharging with the electricity price (price sensor in ct/kWh):
Cheap, below the cheap threshold: tariff charging charges at a fixed power up to the SOC target.
Medium: Tariff Lock, zones 1 and 2 do not discharge.
Expensive, from the expensive threshold: normal operation.

Tariff charging ends at the SOC target or as soon as no cheap price applies any more. On days with a high PV forecast, tariff control can rest entirely. Zone 0 has priority; AC charging and tariff charging exclude each other. With several instances, the others of the grid group only discharge PV during tariff charging. During target charging, tariff charging only starts as an enabled charging source.

dynoff.summary: Dynamic Offset — automatically calculated from grid volatility
dynoff.text:
The dynamic offset adapts the zero-point offset to the restlessness of the grid power. If consumption fluctuates strongly, the offset rises so that load jumps do not lead to export; with a calm grid it falls. It is based on the internally calculated standard deviation of the grid power over the time window.

Formula: offset = clamp(min + max(0, (StdDev − noise) × factor), min, max). Example with min 30, max 250, noise 15 and factor 1.5: StdDev 30 W gives 52 W, StdDev 80 W gives 128 W.

Each zone can be enabled individually and replaces the static offset there. Trimming leaves short load spikes out of the calculation. Several instances on the same grid sensor share one standard deviation.

night.summary: Night Shutdown — disable Zone 2 when PV < PV reserve, re-enable with hysteresis
night.text:
Affects Zone 2 only (case F): output 0 W, timer toggle, rest mode, integral reset.
Zone 1 and AC charging continue running at night.

Off threshold: PV reserve from zone settings. On threshold: PV reserve + hysteresis (default 0 W). In between, the last state is kept.

Reactivation: once PV reaches the on threshold, case E applies (integral reset, timer toggle, mode → '1') — provided no tariff lock is active.

The same darkness (off and on threshold as above) switches the Zone 1 Night Offset (Zones tab) — even with night shutdown disabled.

target.summary: Target charging — charge to the target SOC, then discharge pause
target.text:
Target charging charges the battery to the target SOC and then holds it in the discharge pause, e.g. for storage over the winter or as a precaution before storms.

Charging: the battery charges via the enabled charging sources AC charging, tariff charging and grid charging; Zone 0 is blocked. With house priority PV covers the house first, with battery priority all PV goes into the battery. Grid charging charges from the grid immediately, without a price condition.

Discharge pause: at the target SOC the integration switches regulation off, the device outputs 0 W. The pause survives restarts and only ends when target charging is switched off or “Control active” is switched on.

Target SOC, grid charge power, target charging and grid charging also exist as entities for your own automations.

entities.summary: Entities — every optional sensor assignment for this instance in one place
entities.text:
Bundles the entity-picker fields that would otherwise be scattered across the Zones, Surplus and Tariff tabs. Enable flags and numeric thresholds stay in their respective feature tab — this tab only assigns WHAT is read.

With multiple instances there's also a global default per sensor in the Distribution tab: local (here) overrides global, otherwise the global value applies. If a field is left empty both here and globally, that function has no effect — even if its enable flag is set.

col_descs.entities_all: Optional entity assignments for this instance. Enable flags and numeric thresholds stay in their respective feature tab (Zones, Surplus, Tariff) — this only assigns which entity is read. With multiple instances: local (here) overrides the global value from the Distribution tab, otherwise the global value applies.

pi_enabled.d: On: zones 1 and 2 discharge via the PI controller with P and I factor. Off: setpoint calculation as in AC charging — new setpoint = actual discharge power + (grid − offset), in one step, without integral; while the ramp is running, it only lowers. P and I factor only act when on and are greyed out otherwise. Switching resets the integral.

p_factor.d: Responds immediately to the current deviation (grid − offset). Higher = more aggressive. Too high: output oscillates permanently. Typical after tuning: 0.8–1.5

i_factor.d: Accumulates deviations over time, eliminates steady-state error. Default 0.05. With 0 the PI acts purely proportionally and the integral stays 0. Typical: 0.03–0.08

tolerance.d: Deviations (grid − offset) within this range trigger no control action — neither PI step nor setpoint calculation. With grid import, the output is also not raised while it sits at most one dead band below the zone-1/2 limit. With discharge PI, the integral decay kicks in instead (−5 % per regulation cycle when |integral| > 10). In AC charging the same dead band applies to |AC offset − grid|.

wait_time.d: Compensates the device response time + sensor polling latency after an output change. Without self-adjust: fixed pause. With self-adjust: maximum timeout as safety net.

self_adjust_enabled.d: After each output change, waits for the actual inverter output power. Once actual_power reaches the target ±tolerance, the controller continues. The wait time acts as a maximum timeout.

self_adjust_tolerance.d: Deviation between actual_power and target in watts at which the target is considered reached and the wait ends. Typical: 2–5 W.

zone1_limit.d: SOC exceeds this value → Zone 1 starts. Zone 1 runs through until SOC ≤ Zone 3 threshold — no yo-yo effect. Also active at night.

zone3_limit.d: SOC at or below this value → Zone 3 (safety stop): output 0 W, rest mode. Must be less than Zone 1 threshold. AC charging remains possible despite Zone 3.

pv_reserve.d: Zone-2 output limit: min(Hard Limit Z1, max(0, PV − reserve)) — PV-based limit capped by Hard Limit Z1. Also the off threshold for night shutdown: Zone 2 disabled when PV < reserve (re-enabled at reserve + night hysteresis). Also the switching threshold of the Night Offset. While target charging with house priority, the PV-based limit also applies in Zone 1.

hard_limit_z0.d: Output power ceiling in Zone 0 (surplus feed-in). The inverter is set to this value while surplus is active. Typically the legal maximum (e.g. 800 W). If the optional export-limit entity is configured, max(Z0, Z1) is written to it in every regulation cycle. Can also be set via the entity “Zone 0 limit”.

hard_limit_z1.d: Output power ceiling in Zone 1 (discharge) and Zone 2 (PV tracking). In Zone 2 the combined limit min(hard limit Z1, max(0, PV − reserve)) applies. If PV drops suddenly, discharge control keeps running and corrects output downward. Can also be set via the entity “Zone 1/2 limit”, e.g. to limit the discharge power at night by automation.

discharge_max.d: Discharge current in Zone 1 and at rest in mode 0. Zone 2, rest in mode 1, AC charging, tariff charging and grid charging automatically set 0 A. Surplus sets 2 A.

offset_1.d: Control target in Zone 1. Positive = controller maintains slight grid import as safety buffer. Negative = controller slightly exports. Overridden when dynamic offset for Zone 1 is active. Replaced by the Night Offset while dark, if enabled.

z1_night_enabled.d: In the Zone 1 cycle, replaces the Zone-1 offset with the Night Offset while it is dark, static or dynamic (Dyn. Offset tab, column Zone 1 Night). Darkness starts at PV < PV reserve and ends at PV ≥ PV reserve + re-enable hysteresis (Night tab); no time of day, independent of night shutdown.

offset_1_night.d: Control target in Zone 1 while it is dark, e.g. positive for slight grid import instead of exporting battery energy. Overridden when dynamic offset for Zone 1 Night is active.

offset_2.d: Control target in Zone 2. Recommended: slightly larger than Zone-1 offset (stronger import buffer when battery is discharged conservatively). Overridden when dynamic offset for Zone 2 is active.

surplus_enabled.d: Zone 0: feeds in at Hard Limit Z0 with a full battery and PV surplus. Highest priority after charging to the target, blocks tariff charging, Tariff Lock and AC charging. Entry from the export threshold and PV surplus; with forecast also earlier (see below).

surplus_soc_threshold.d: Zone 0 only starts at this SOC. Must be above the zone-1 threshold — otherwise regulation pauses with an error message. Recommendation: ~5 % below the app charge limit (e.g. 95 % with max 100 %) — entry is only measurable while the battery is still charging; at the full-charge point the hardware throttles PV down to consumption and the surplus becomes invisible.

surplus_soc_hyst.d: Exit only when SOC < (threshold − hysteresis). Prevents flickering near the threshold. Typical: 3–5 %.

surplus_pv_hyst.d: Entry: PV > delivery + grid + hysteresis. Exit: PV ≤ actual power + grid − hysteresis. In the discharge pool of a grid group the hysteresis is scaled by the error share, an instance outside the pool counts unscaled — the dead band stays proportional to the consumption reference.

surplus_forecast_enabled.d: With forecast ≥ threshold, Zone 0 starts as soon as PV > Hard Limit Z0 and SOC > zone 3, without export threshold. While all three conditions hold, the exit is blocked; once one drops away, the normal exit (SOC or consumption) applies.

surplus_forecast_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "PV Forecast Today" entity (Entities tab) this function stays inactive — shared field with the tariff PV forecast.

surplus_forecast_threshold.d: PV > Hard Limit Z0 + forecast ≥ threshold + SOC > zone-3 threshold → surplus starts without export threshold and stays active while all three conditions hold.

surplus_lock_enabled.d: Keeps Zone 0 through short PV dips while the power forecast is ≥ lock factor × Hard Limit Z0: the PV exit is blocked, the SOC exit stays active. If the sensor permanently reports too much, Zone 0 stays active until the SOC exit.

surplus_lock_sensor.d: Sensor with the currently forecast PV power in W (e.g. Solcast power_now, k-units normalized ×1000 automatically). Feeds the exit lock for Zone 0 (Surplus tab).

surplus_lock_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "Power Forecast Sensor" entity (Entities tab) this lock stays inactive.

surplus_lock_factor.d: Lock active while forecast ≥ factor × Hard Limit Z0. Higher factor = more safety margin against forecast errors. Default: 1.5.

ac_enabled.d: Charges the battery when power would be exported at the grid connection even without own discharging (case G). Ends at the charge target or once the surplus is gone (case H). Does not start during Zone 0 or tariff charging; Zone 3 keeps protecting.

ac_soc_target.d: Charging stops when SOC reaches this value. Recommended: > Zone-1 threshold — so Zone 1 takes over directly after charging and runs zero-export.

ac_power_limit.d: Absolute ceiling for AC charge power. If the output power is above it, it is lowered immediately.

ac_min_power.d: Smallest charge setpoint that is written; if the setpoint calculation yields less, 0 is written. Values below 50 W oscillate — the device does not hold smaller charge powers steady. 0 disables the threshold. If the value exceeds the max. charge power, the max. charge power serves as the threshold.

ac_hysteresis.d: Margin around the offset for entry and exit of AC charging; prevents toggling at the boundary.

ac_offset.d: Control target for grid power in mode 3 (AC charging). Negative = export targeted; the charge power is calculated from grid and actual power so that the grid hits this value. Overridden when dynamic offset for Zone AC is active.

tariff_enabled.d: Cheap (< cheap threshold): tariff charging. Below the expensive threshold (cheap and medium): Tariff Lock — Zone 1 and Zone 2 blocked. Expensive (≥ expensive threshold): normal SOC logic. Blocked while surplus feed-in (Zone 0) is active. Independent of the AC charging module.

tariff_price_sensor.d: Sensor entity with the current electricity price in ct/kWh. Feeds tariff arbitrage (Tariff tab).

tariff_price_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "Price Sensor" entity (Entities tab) tariff arbitrage stays inactive.

tariff_cheap_threshold.d: Tariff charging starts when price is below this threshold AND SOC < target − SOC hysteresis. Below it the Tariff Lock still applies once the charge target is reached.

tariff_cheap_entity.d: Optional entity (sensor, input_number or number), overrides the static cheap threshold. Feeds tariff arbitrage (Tariff tab).

tariff_exp_threshold.d: Above this threshold: normal SOC logic, Tariff Lock lifts. Below it: Tariff Lock Zone 1 and Zone 2. Should be above the cheap threshold (not checked).

tariff_exp_entity.d: Optional entity (sensor, input_number or number), overrides the static expensive threshold. Feeds tariff arbitrage (Tariff tab).

tariff_dynamic_entities_note.d: 🔌 Optional "Dynamic Cheap Threshold" / "Dynamic Expensive Threshold" entities (Entities tab) override the numeric values above when set. If such an entity has no numeric value, the value above applies, with a warning.

tariff_soc_target.d: Tariff charging stops when this SOC is reached. Independent of the AC charging module's SOC target.

tariff_soc_hyst.d: Tariff charging only starts when SOC < (charge target − hysteresis). Prevents toggling between tariff charging and Tariff Lock at the charge target. 0 = start right below the charge target.

tariff_power.d: Fixed charge power during tariff charging — no PI controller, no dynamic adjustment.

pv_forecast_enabled.d: When active and the forecast sensor reports a value ≥ threshold, tariff charging and Tariff Lock are suppressed. Automatic flexibility for sunny days.

pv_forecast_sensor.d: input_number or sensor entity with the expected kWh yield today (e.g. weather integration or Solcast account; Wh/MWh normalized to kWh automatically). Feeds the forecast suppression of tariff charging and Tariff Lock (Tariff tab), Surplus Forecast Override (Surplus tab) and, between 0–12h, Zone-1 Night Forcing (Zones tab).

pv_forecast_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "PV Forecast Today" entity (Entities tab) this function stays inactive.

pv_forecast_threshold.d: When forecast ≥ this value: tariff charging and Tariff Lock are blocked, normal zero-export continues.

zone1_force_enabled.d: Allows the Zone-1 discharge cycle to start even below the normal Zone-1 threshold when the target day's PV yield refills the battery. Only the entry is brought forward; the exit still runs through the Zone-3 threshold. Only applies while it is dark (PV < PV reserve) and SOC is above its own minimum SOC (below).

zone1_force_sensor.d: input_number or sensor entity with the expected kWh yield for tomorrow (Wh/MWh are normalised to kWh); used from 12:00 to midnight. From 0:00 to 12:00 the Zone 1 night forcing uses "PV forecast today" for the same day instead.

zone1_force_sensor_note.d: 🔌 Without the "PV Forecast Tomorrow" entity (Entities tab) this function stays inactive.

zone1_force_threshold.d: Forcing only applies once the PV forecast for the target day reaches or exceeds this value.

zone1_force_min_soc.d: Dedicated safety floor for Night Forcing, independent of the Zone-3 threshold (which only governs the regular exit). Must lie strictly between the Zone-3 and Zone-1 thresholds — prevents forcing at SOC values where the state-of-charge estimate becomes unreliable.

stddev_window.d: Time window for the standard deviation calculation. Each grid sensor report counts once; control cycles without a new report add nothing. Applies to all zones.

stddev_trim_count.d: Number of the highest and of the lowest values in the StdDev window that are left out per side before the calculation; 5 therefore leaves out 10 values. Filters short load spikes, such as inrush currents, out of the dynamic offset. 0 = no trimming (default).

dyn_z1_enabled.d: Calculates the offset dynamically from the grid StdDev instead of the static value. Overrides the static Zone-1 offset.

dyn_z1_min.d: Base buffer with a calm grid (StdDev ≤ noise threshold). Offset never falls below this value.

dyn_z1_max.d: Upper ceiling of the offset. Offset never exceeds this value, even at very high StdDev.

dyn_z1_noise.d: StdDev below this threshold is treated as measurement noise and does not trigger an offset increase.

dyn_z1_factor.d: Gain above the noise threshold. Formula: buffer = (StdDev − noise) × factor.

dyn_z1_negative.d: Negates the calculated offset (× −1). The control target then lies below 0 W.

dyn_z1_night_enabled.d: Calculates the Night Offset dynamically from the grid StdDev instead of the static Night Offset. Only effective while the Night Offset is enabled (Zones tab).

dyn_z1_night_min.d: Base buffer with a calm grid (StdDev ≤ noise threshold). Offset never falls below this value.

dyn_z1_night_max.d: Upper ceiling of the offset. Offset never exceeds this value, even at very high StdDev.

dyn_z1_night_noise.d: StdDev below this threshold is treated as measurement noise and does not trigger an offset increase.

dyn_z1_night_factor.d: Gain above the noise threshold. Formula: buffer = (StdDev − noise) × factor.

dyn_z1_night_negative.d: Negates the calculated offset (× −1). The control target then lies below 0 W.

dyn_z2_enabled.d: Calculates the offset dynamically from the grid StdDev instead of the static value. Overrides the static Zone-2 offset.

dyn_z2_min.d: Base buffer with a calm grid (StdDev ≤ noise threshold). Offset never falls below this value.

dyn_z2_max.d: Upper ceiling of the offset. Offset never exceeds this value, even at very high StdDev.

dyn_z2_noise.d: StdDev below this threshold is treated as measurement noise and does not trigger an offset increase.

dyn_z2_factor.d: Gain above the noise threshold. Formula: buffer = (StdDev − noise) × factor.

dyn_z2_negative.d: Negates the calculated offset (× −1). The control target then lies below 0 W.

dyn_ac_enabled.d: Calculates the AC charge offset dynamically from the grid StdDev instead of the static value. Overrides the static AC offset.

dyn_ac_min.d: Base buffer with a calm grid (StdDev ≤ noise threshold). Offset never falls below this value.

dyn_ac_max.d: Upper ceiling of the offset. Offset never exceeds this value, even at very high StdDev.

dyn_ac_noise.d: StdDev below this threshold is treated as measurement noise and does not trigger an offset increase.

dyn_ac_factor.d: Gain above the noise threshold. Formula: buffer = (StdDev − noise) × factor.

dyn_ac_negative.d: Negates the calculated offset (× −1). The control target then lies below 0 W.

night_enabled.d: Disable Zone 2 when PV < PV reserve. Zone 1 and AC charging continue running. Zone 2 is not reactivated while a Tariff Lock (medium/cheap price) is active.

night_hysteresis.d: Night ends only once PV ≥ PV reserve + hysteresis; it still starts at PV < PV reserve. 0 = on and off threshold identical. Also applies to the Night Offset.

target_charge_enabled.d: Same value as the switch “Target charging”. On: regulation on, charge to the target SOC, then discharge pause. Off: normal operation, regulation on, grid charging off.

target_charge_note.d: 🎯 Target reached (case ZE) → regulation off: discharge pause. It only ends via target charging off or “Control active” on. Target SOC and charging sources can be set while target charging is off.

target_soc.d: Charging ends at this SOC, then the discharge pause follows. Default 70 %: the battery is stored in the middle charge range, which is gentle on the cells over weeks, and keeps a reserve against self-discharge. The device's max. SOC remains the upper bound — a target above it is never reached. Can also be set via the entity “Target SOC”. A change applies immediately while charging, during the discharge pause only after target charging is switched on again.

target_battery_priority.d: Off (house priority, default): Zone 1 and Zone 2 run, the output power is capped to PV − PV reserve even with an active cycle; the battery only charges PV above house consumption. On (battery priority, case ZB): output 0 W in rest mode, all PV charges the battery, the house draws from the grid.

target_source_ac.d: AC charging (case G) may start while charging to the target; the switch in the AC tab must be on as well. Off: no AC charging while charging to the target, a running session ends (case H).

target_source_tariff.d: Tariff charging (case GT) may start while charging to the target; the switch in the tariff tab must be on as well. Off: no tariff charging while charging to the target, a running session ends (case HT).

target_grid_charge.d: Same value as the switch “Grid charging”. While charging to the target, charges from the grid immediately at the grid charging power, without a price condition, until charging ends (cases GN/HN, at the target SOC case ZE). Switches off when target charging ends.

target_grid_power.d: Fixed charge power of grid charging, independent of the max. charge power of AC charging. Default 800 W like max. charge power and tariff charge power: with default values grid charging charges at the same power as AC and tariff charging. Can also be set via the entity “Grid charging power”.

periodic_enabled.d: Runs the regulation loop at a fixed interval — even without sensor changes. Useful for stable households where grid power rarely fluctuates, and for setups without PV panels on the device, where the solar sensor never fires.

periodic_interval.d: Seconds between periodic regulation runs. Minimum: 5 s.

remote_timeout.d: Time after which, according to the specification, the device falls back to the app settings without a new remote control command. The regulation renews it once the countdown drops below 120 s. Default 3599 s, minimum 300 s.

top_card.title: ⚡ Solakon ONE Zero Export
top_card.p1: The Solakon ONE Zero Export integration automatically controls the inverter output power so that grid import is kept as close to 0 W as possible — without exporting to the public grid.
top_card.p2: At its core is a PI controller with grid power as the controlled variable and inverter output power as the manipulated variable; in discharge optionally a setpoint calculation on actual basis. Behaviour is governed by four SOC zones: Zone 1 discharges aggressively, Zone 2 conservatively, Zone 3 blocks discharge, Zone 0 actively exports surplus.
top_card.p3: Optional modules: ☀️ Surplus, ⚡ AC charging, 💹 Tariff Arbitrage, 📈 Dynamic Offset (per zone individually), 🌙 Night Shutdown, 🎯 Target Charging. All parameters are stored persistently here in the panel — no YAML, no helper entities.
top_card.prio_heading: Priority and mutual blocking of optional modules:
prio_rows: Surplus (0A); AC charge (G) and tariff charge (GT) without enabled source; with battery priority Zone-1/2-start (A, E)
Tariff charge (GT), Tariff Lock (TM), AC charge (G)
top_card.prio_note: AC charging and tariff charging mutually block each other via the mode guard (mode ≠ '3'). Surplus feed-in takes precedence over all other optional modules — none can start while Zone 0 is active. Only charging to the target locks surplus; grid charging takes precedence over tariff charging.

status.instances_load_error: Instances could not be loaded — reopen the page.

debug.pi_desc: Manually resets the I-part of the PI controller to 0. Useful after a manual intervention.
debug.zone_desc: Manually switches the cycle, resets the integral and toggles the timer.
debug.rest_desc: While control rests (zone 3, night, Tariff Lock, battery priority, charge end without cycle, case I in mode '3' without charge session and without cycle, return to mode 1 during Tariff Lock or battery priority, recovery after a stall), the device stays in mode '1' at 0 W instead of mode '0'. Only for devices that do not charge in mode '0' despite the app settings (0 W default output, no smart meter).
debug.rest_warn: Not recommended hack: the device only leaves remote control when control is switched off.

dist.single_instance_note: Power distribution is only needed with multiple instances on the same grid power sensor.
dist.groups_note: Instances are grouped automatically by their configured grid power sensor — each grid group (e.g. multiple smart meters for separate circuits) gets its own, independent power distribution. With only one group this grouping is invisible, there's just a single shared pool. The displayed name is the Home Assistant area of the grid sensor, otherwise its display name.
dist.load_error: Could not load the distribution — reopen the page.
dist.global_max_desc: Absolute ceiling for all instances combined — split according to weights, and it also applies while only one instance is discharging. If an instance is capped by its own hard limit (Zones tab), the unused remainder is automatically passed on to instances with headroom (water-filling) — otherwise the pool would never reach this value with unevenly sized instances. Default: 800 W (legal feed-in maximum). Can also be set via the entity “Total max. output power” on the device “Solakon grid group N”; N is shown at the top of this page.
dist.global_max_inactive: The total limit only takes effect once a second instance of this grid group is running. The value is saved.
dist.cap_sensor_desc: Battery capacity sensor (in kWh) per instance — used to weight the power split in "Capacity-weighted" mode. The dot next to the field shows entity validity live: green = provides a number, amber = exists but unknown/unavailable or not numeric, red = does not exist (check for typos):
dist.mode_desc:
Equal → each active instance (mode '1', zero feed-in) receives the same share
SOC-weighted → instance with more usable energy (SOC above minimum) gets more power, regardless of battery size — SOC values equalise over time
Capacity-weighted → like SOC-weighted, additionally × battery capacity (kWh) — useful with differently sized batteries, so the SOC of all instances drops at the same rate. Requires a valid capacity sensor per instance below.
SOC-switching → only one instance discharges at a time, exclusively (100 %), the others sit idle. Hands over to the instance with the highest remaining SOC once the active one has dropped by the divergence threshold — instances are worked through one after another instead of drawing on all of them in parallel.

AC charging has its own, independent distribution pool (see the "AC Charge" tab), weighted there by the room left to the charge target.

If, under SOC-weighted/Capacity-weighted/SOC-switching, another instance's SOC sensor is currently unavailable, the pool falls back to equal distribution for that regulation cycle; if only a capacity is missing under Capacity-weighted, it falls back to SOC-weighted — shown as a message in the status/error field, never a silent fallback.
dist.soc_switch_divergence_desc: The active instance discharges exclusively until its SOC has dropped by this value since taking over — then the instance with the highest remaining SOC takes over. Smaller values = more frequent switching, finer equalisation; larger values = less frequent switching, each instance discharges further down in one go. If the active instance was briefly in Zone 0 (surplus feed-in), the threshold is re-anchored to the current SOC once it leaves Zone 0 — so that period doesn't count twice against the budget.
dist.global_sensors_desc: Cross-instance default for sensors that typically apply to the whole household (one weather/Solcast account, one electricity tariff) — each instance can optionally override locally in the Entities tab, otherwise this value applies. The dot next to each field shows entity validity live (green/amber/red).
dist.global_pv_today_desc: Feeds the Surplus Forecast Override (Surplus tab), the forecast suppression of tariff charging and Tariff Lock (Tariff tab) and, between 0–12h, Zone-1 Night Forcing (Zones tab), unless an instance overrides it locally.
dist.global_pv_tomorrow_desc: Feeds the Zone-1 Night Forcing (Zones tab). Read from noon to midnight; from 0 to 12h "PV Forecast Today" above is used automatically instead (same target day).
dist.global_surplus_lock_desc: Feeds the Zone-0 exit lock (Surplus tab), unless an instance overrides it locally.
dist.global_tariff_price_desc: Feeds the tariff arbitrage (Tariff tab), unless an instance overrides it locally.
dist.global_tariff_cheap_desc: Optional entity (sensor, input_number or number), overrides the static cheap threshold, unless an instance overrides it locally.
dist.global_tariff_exp_desc: Optional entity (sensor, input_number or number), overrides the static expensive threshold, unless an instance overrides it locally.
